title: A Novel Tenorrhaphy Suture Technique with Tissue Engineered Collagen Graft to Repair Large Tendon Defects
protocol: Add 4 mL of rat tail collagen type 1 monomeric collagen solution (2.15 mg/mL in 0.6% acetic acid) and 500 μL of 10x Minimal Essential Medium.
Neutralize the mixture by titrating against 5 M and 1 M sodium hydroxide.
Add 500 μL of Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM).
Pour 5 mL of this solution into a custom-built rectangular metal mold (33 mm × 22 mm × 10 mm, 120 g weight).
Keep the mold in a CO2 incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 15 minutes to allow matrix assembly.
Remove the collagen hydrogel from the mold after polymerization.
Place the collagen hydrogel in a standard plastic compression assembly.
Place the collagen hydrogel between two 50 µm nylon mesh sheets.
Apply a static load of 120 g for 5 minutes to remove interstitial fluid from the hydrogel.
Absorb discharged fluid with four layers of filter paper.
Cut four compressed gel layers into 15 mm segments.
Sedate animals with an intramuscular dose of Hypnorm.
Euthanize animals by administering pentobarbitone.
Trim hair on both hind legs.
Make a 9 cm incision to expose the tibialis posterior tendon.
Excise lapine TP tendons and keep moist in PBS.
With a surgical blade, cut the TP tendon at the midpoint.
Excise a 15 mm segment of the tendon from the middle of the tendon.
Replace the excised segment with an ET collagen graft.
Interlock the 3-0 suture proximally away from native tendon ends.
Pass the 3-0 core sutures above the entire length of the graft.
Interlock the 3-0 core sutures distally away from the cut end.
Secure both ends of the ET to the native tendon with 6-0 and continuous running sutures around the periphery by coupling two tendon ends.
Manually ensure that the tension on the sutures is appropriate.
